points.minimum: States that adding a new series to an existing trust by a Rule 485(a) post-effective amendment normally becomes automatically effective 75 days after filing. States that this is a filing-effectiveness clock, not a promised launch date. Optional subdetails: other material 485(a) amendments normally use 60 days; the registrant may designate a later effective date; the SEC may accelerate effectiveness; a citation to Rule 485(a)(1)–(3).

Cites a filed example, such as Simplify's January 30, 2024 485APOS cover, that elects the 75-day route and states that shares cannot be sold before effectiveness. The general principle that shares cannot be sold before effectiveness is acceptable without naming the example.

Explains why 75 days is not an end-to-end launch guarantee. Names at least one source of extra time outside the filing clock: preparatory work, exchange or listing and operational readiness, or separate exemptive relief where needed. Must also distinguish a new trust: it does not use the Rule 485(a) post-effective-amendment route, and the 75-day clock is not the rule for its initial registration. Optional subdetail: a designated later effective date for a new-series amendment may be at most 95 days after filing. A specific commercial launch-time estimate is not required and should not be presented as verified.

central_errors: States that the normal automatic-effectiveness period for adding a new series by 485(a) amendment is 60 days, or another figure other than 75 days.
Presents 75 days, or any filing period, as a guaranteed or binding end-to-end launch or trading deadline.
States that shares may be offered or sold before the amendment becomes effective.
Applies the Rule 485(a) 75-day post-effective-amendment clock to a new trust's initial registration statement, or says the two follow the same process.
States that a new series can be added effective immediately on filing under Rule 485(b) as the normal route.
Presents an unverified universal commercial launch timeline as an established rule.

scoring_rule.correct: Meets the minimum for both required points (1 and 3), including the 75-day figure, the filing-clock-not-launch-guarantee distinction, at least one extra time factor, and the new-trust distinction. Contains no central error. Optional points are not needed for full credit.
scoring_rule.partial: Gives the correct 75-day period with no central error, but only partly covers point 3: for example, it gives the non-guarantee caveat or extra time factors but omits the new-trust distinction, or the reverse. Award half credit for each required point covered only in part. Omissions alone never make an answer wrong.
scoring_rule.wrong: Contains any central error, or fails to identify 75 days as the normal period for a new-series 485(a) amendment, whether by giving no period or a wrong one.
